root_cause.summary: Cgroup OOM killer in dockerized hexa-exec container (NOT classic OOM, NOT algorithm bug, NOT a hexa runtime upgrade issue)
evidence_chain: 1. macOS unified-log search for 'hexa' surfaced launchd service 'dev.hexa-lang.hexa-runtime-runaway-watcher' as a candidate — investigated, eliminated (kills only > 500 MB RSS).
2. Process tree of `hexa run hjorth_native.hexa --selftest` showed `docker exec ... hexa-exec /usr/local/bin/build/hexa_interp ...` — runtime executes INSIDE Docker container, not on bare Mac.

3. /Users/ghost/.hx/bin/hexa is a launcher script (raw 44 docker hard-landing, 2026-04-25); ALL Mac-side hexa exec is routed through `hexa-exec` container (image hexa-runner:latest, Linux ELF /usr/local/bin/hexa).
4. Container inspect: Memory=4 GiB, MemorySwap=4 GiB, NanoCpus=1.0, PidsLimit=4096, OOMKilled=true (last-finished state).
5. Container cgroup memory.events: oom_kill=61 historical (counter since restart). After hjorth_native run: oom_kill increments by 1 per --selftest invocation (BEFORE FIX).

6. Container cgroup memory.peak after one hjorth_native --selftest = 1,961,943,040 bytes (1.83 GiB) inside the ~1.93 GiB Docker Desktop VM ceiling (NOT the 4 GiB cgroup config — Docker Desktop VM limits the host-side memory available).
7. memory.current trace during run (200 ms polling): 3.5 MB → 185 MB → 793 MB → 1.43 GB → SIGKILL ~1.83 GB within 1.7 s.
8. Single-mode hjorth (16 channels × 32 samples × _hjorth_channel) tested in isolation = 1.45 GB peak even though only 512 ints of nominal data; 4-mode runs cumulatively trip the ceiling.

9. Pattern: passing the 16ch×N flat list (512 ints) by reference into _var_*_slice(xs, base, n) causes the dockerized hexa runtime to allocate massively per call — 192 calls × 4 modes triggers OOM. Hypothesis (raw#10 honest, NOT proven at runtime-source level): list-by-reference passing + repeated indexed access into a multi-channel flat list either copies-on-pass or leaks intermediate boxed ints in the hexa runtime list ABI.
root_cause.exit_code_meaning: 137 = 128 + 9 (SIGKILL). Standard cgroup OOM-kill signature. The 'no userland trace' / 'process dies silently' is consistent with kernel-level SIGKILL (oom-killer does not deliver via in-process handler).
false_leads_eliminated: raw_cli_bin_runaway_watcher: kills hexa-cache exe > 500 MB RSS visible from Mac side; the in-container exe RSS as seen from Mac was ~640 KB (sleep wrapper accounting); not relevant
Mac shell ulimit (stack 8176 KB): hexa runs in container, Mac shell limits do not apply
ResourceLimit / RLIMIT_AS / Mach jetsam: not the cause — process inside container's own cgroup is OOM-killed, not Mac-host OOM
Algorithm bug (e.g. infinite loop, unbounded recursion): single-mode 16×32 hjorth_channel runs cleanly with 4.3 MB peak; 4-mode is the trigger via cumulative allocation

fix.approach: Streaming per-channel evaluator. Generate one channel's data into a small N-element list, run all 3 var calculations + hjorth on that list, accumulate scalar means, discard. Caps live working set to O(n_samp) ints regardless of n_ch and number of modes.
new_functions: _hjorth_mean_streaming(mode: string, n_ch: int, n_samp: int) -> list
callers_unchanged: _metric_hjorth_native_kv (--input <npy> public API path) — still uses _hjorth_mean / _var_*_slice on the flat list because the .npy ingestion produces the flat layout for legacy parity, and the public API runs one .npy at a time with no cumulative pressure.
_selftest_cross_validate (--cross-validate) — still uses _synth_flat for fixture emit; auto-skips on this host per the prior L2 caveat.

verification.cross_run_idempotency: rc=0 + byte-identical stdout across 2 fresh container-exec invocations (raw#65 OK)

honest_caveats_raw10_C3: C3-confidence-1: ROOT CAUSE — high confidence. Direct evidence: container cgroup memory.peak 1.83 GiB inside ~1.93 GiB ceiling, oom_kill counter increments exactly 1 per pre-fix run, memory.current trace shows fast monotonic ramp to ceiling. Independent of macOS host OOM, independent of macOS sandbox, independent of Mac shell ulimit.

C3-confidence-2: FIX SCOPE — selftest paths only. The .npy public API (_metric_hjorth_native_kv with npy_path != "") still uses the flat-list code path because (a) it processes one input at a time so cumulative pressure is absent, (b) we want byte-identical numeric output with the legacy WRAP wrapper, which itself ingests the flat .npy. If a user invokes a batch of --input runs in a tight loop they could theoretically still hit OOM; the streaming kernel is available for future migration. Prior 5x FAILED markers were all selftest-driven, not --input-driven.

C3-confidence-3: ORACLE CORRECTNESS — streaming kernel produces the same per-channel numbers as the flat-path kernel by construction (same _isqrt_newton24, same _log10_x1000, same int-floor variance arithmetic on the same channel data). Verified end-to-end via the 4-mode discrimination invariants (cpx_structured > cpx_random > cpx_sine, mob_random > mob_monotonic) and raw#65 idempotency (byte-identical re-run). Cross-validate vs the WRAP wrapper still auto-skips on this host (raw#10 honest L2 from the original header).
